logs: Shortlist: Theervu, OruKural, Sollu, Nilai — DHO Review Copilot, Kanakku, PayirDesk, VeppaNadi

shortlist.name: Theervu
painsCovered: Flat FIFO queue — no de-duplication or evidence-based ranking of what is genuinely most urgent
Ghost closures — 'resolved' with no work — make official priority data untrustworthy
Citizens/staff can't get a grounded answer on status, who-is-responsible, or timelines
Unstructured Tamil/Tanglish grievances arrive messy (partial: it normalizes the export)
shortlist.universalCore: A messy-complaint-stream → trustworthy-ranked-priorities + accountability-report engine: embed-dedup, trust-corrected ranking, and an anomaly layer that treats the official 'resolved' flag as adversarial data. shortlist.oneLiner: An officer's decision cockpit that de-dupes messy grievances into ranked ward priorities and exposes fake closures — showing the true unresolved load instead of a flat FIFO queue.

result.diversityNote: Spread covers all four tracks: Institutions (Theervu, Sollu), Health (OruKural, Nilai), Zero Hunger (Kanakku, PayirDesk), Cities/Climate (VeppaNadi). On the SCALABILITY lens the shortlist deliberately front-loads language/geography-agnostic cores — Theervu (any grievance system), OruKural (any CHW documentation burden), Kanakku (any informal-economy credit passport, the single most scalable core, TAM-wise) and PayirDesk (any field-expert teletriage ratio) all generalize far beyond Tamil; VeppaNadi is the outlier at scalability 3 because its moat is a telemedicine data partnership that's harder to templatize (kept for track balance and builder-specific defensibility). On the COVERAGE lens there's an intentional split: Theervu (4) and the platform-style Kanakku/Nilai/PayirDesk/Sollu (3) are the 'knock out multiple pains' plays, while OruKural (2) and VeppaNadi (2) are single-pain-done-brilliantly picks — included because fit/wow/pilot credibility can outweigh breadth for a first-time hackathon deploy. The top pick (Theervu) is the only concept that scores high on BOTH co-primary axes simultaneously, which is why it leads. Every shortlisted item is demoable as one hero flow in 36hr; Kanakku and (rejected) Saatchi are the two most at risk of scope overreach if the full platform is attempted instead of the single slice.

# Theervu — Build Spec
**Track:** AI for Strong Institutions · **Tag:** Broadest Coverage

**Pitch:** An officer's decision cockpit that de-dupes messy grievances into ranked ward priorities and exposes fake "resolved" closures — showing the *true unresolved load* instead of a flat FIFO queue.

**Universal core vs Tamil launch locale:** The product is a language- and geography-agnostic intelligence tier: *messy complaint stream → trust-corrected ranked priorities + accountability report*. Embed-dedup, evidence-based ranking, and an anomaly layer that treats the official `resolved` flag as adversarial data are what any 311/grievance system on earth needs. Tamil + Coimbatore PGRS/CM-Helpline is only the launch locale and seed dataset — swap the corpus, the engine ports.

**Pains it covers (the breadth story):**
- Flat FIFO queue → evidence-based ranking of what's genuinely urgent
- Ghost closures ("resolved" with no work) → recomputed *True Unresolved Load*
- No grounded answer on status/owner/timeline → RAG attaches owning officer + statutory SLA
- Messy Tamil/Tanglish intake → normalized, clustered problems (partial: normalizes the export)

**Evidence (1 hard point):** TN runs CM Helpline (1100) and the PGRS portal receiving lakhs of grievances across phone, web, WhatsApp and paper — with no cross-channel de-duplication, so one pothole reported 40 times reads as 40 tickets, and closures are compiled by hand into monthly aging reports. (Directionally verified; exact figures pending ULB export.)

**Who uses it + core loop:** Municipal zonal/ward officers, DHOs, councillor/MLA back-offices — the *admin* intelligence layer, not citizen intake. Loop: ingest export → embed+cluster → score+explain → officer triages → auto-report.

**AI stack:** Gemini text-embedding-004 (location+issue de-dup/clustering) · Gemini Flash (dept/urgency classification, "why-ranked" + report narrative, TA/EN) · Gemini Vision (proof-photo plausibility + EXIF geo cross-check for ghost-closure detection) · Bhashini Tamil ASR (voice→text intake) · lightweight RAG over jurisdiction charters + SOP timelines.

**36hr MVP slice (hero flow):** Single ward, seeded Tamil/Tanglish CSV mimicking PGRS fields. Embed→cluster→classify→**ranked dashboard** (top ~10 problems: report-count, owning officer, SLA clock, why-ranked). Bolt on ghost-closure detection on a demo subset → headline *True Unresolved Load* → one-click TA+EN aging PDF. *Built:* the pipeline. *Vision:* multi-ward, live PGRS feed, callback verification.

**90-sec wow:** Officer opens cockpit — raw FIFO queue vs Theervu's trustworthy ranked list *side by side* — a fast-closure flag fires, unresolved load jumps, PDF exports in Tamil.

**Global scale path + TAM:** Every ULB, state helpline, and national 311 needs a trust-and-ranking tier over existing intake. TN has 600+ local bodies; India ~4,000+ ULBs; then other states/languages, then any country with a grievance backend (US 311, GovTech markets). GovTech SaaS, normalization+intelligence layer — no rip-and-replace.

**Pilot/incubation:** Read-only over one Coimbatore Corporation zone via existing export (low political friction). GDG technical enablement · TiE Kovai mentors validate scoring weights with a real zonal officer · councillor office = first report user · Startup Culture incubation.

**Why it wins / risks:** Everyone builds intake classifiers; almost no one attacks *data trust* — the ghost-closure layer and True Unresolved Load are the edge. **Risks:** gated ULB data (demo on synthetic), politically sensitive flags (frame as "verify," human-in-loop), colloquial Tamil geo-extraction errors, vision proof is heuristic (needs EXIF+callback), slow govt procurement.

# OruKural — Build Spec
**Track:** AI for Good Health & Well-being · **Tag:** Best Domain Fit · Scalability 4/5 · Pain 2/5

**Pitch:** A Tamil voice-first, offline PWA where a frontline health worker speaks one sentence per patient and it fans out into every register summary plus government-app-ready payloads (HMIS/ANMOL/Ni-Kshay) — killing the double-entry tax.

**Universal core vs Tamil launch locale:** The product is a *capture-once, fan-out-to-many* layer for over-documented community health workers — a global phenomenon (WHO/CHW programs across Africa, LatAm, South Asia). The unit of work is a spoken sentence; a deterministic templating engine fans it into any downstream register/payload. Universal: the voice→structured→multi-export pipeline. Locale-only: the ASR language (Tamil) and the export templates (ANC + ANMOL/HMIS). Swap those two and it ships anywhere.

**Pains it covers:**
- Ends the double-entry tax — one Tamil voice/OCR capture writes every register + govt-app payload.
- Seeds follow-up worklist (partial) — captured next-visit dates auto-populate defaulter tracking.

**Evidence:** Field time-use surveys peg 30–50% of an ANM's working hours on redundant recording rather than care — the same encounter is hand-copied into 10–15 registers, then re-typed into ANMOL/RCH/HMIS.

**Who uses it + core loop:** Rural TN ASHAs/ANMs/PHC nurses (and their MO who consumes summaries). Loop: speak or snap → structured fields → read-back confirm → commit → every register row + export payload populates.

**AI stack:** Bhashini Tamil ASR (on-device Whisper-small fallback offline) → Gemini 2.x Flash structured extraction (strict schema, per-field confidence, handles Tanglish) → Gemini vision OCR for the snap-the-page path → Bhashini TTS read-back. Export/fan-out is **deterministic templating, not AI** — auditable numbers a Medical Officer can trust.

**36hr MVP slice:** ONE hero flow — an ANC visit. Mic → one Tamil sentence → extract {name, visit#, gestational month, anaemia flag, next-visit} → card + TTS read-back → commit → three register rows + downloadable ANMOL/HMIS JSON+CSV all populate. Airplane-mode two more captures, restore network, watch the sync queue drain. Breadth (multi-encounter, dedup, Ni-Kshay) shown as vision, not built.

**90-sec wow:** "Capture once → five artefacts → offline→sync," live, in Tamil.

**Global scale path + TAM:** ~1M ASHAs + ~0.2M ANMs in India; every state = new templates only. Beyond: CHW programs in Kenya, Nigeria, Indonesia, Brazil — swap ASR + export. Buyer: NHM state IT cells, then ministries of health / global-health NGOs (Gates, PATH).

**Pilot/incubation:** 3–5 sub-centres under one Coimbatore PHC block via TiE Kovai + District MO; metric = documentation minutes saved + register-vs-app mismatch reduction over 6 weeks. Start CSV-export only (no API approval needed); graduate to official HMIS/ANMOL push via NHM MoU. GDG for offline hardening; Startup Culture for incubation.

**Why it wins / risks:** Wins by fitting the *existing* paper+ANMOL reality instead of replacing it — voice-first, offline-first, deterministic exports where rivals are form-first/English/online. Risks: code-mixed medical ASR accuracy (mitigate: read-back + term lexicon); gated govt APIs (mitigate: CSV-first); dedup mis-merges (keep suggested + reversible); patient-data privacy (on-device fallback, encryption at rest).

# Sollu — Build Spec
**Track:** AI for Strong Institutions · **Tag:** Boldest · Scalability 4/5 · Pain 3/5

**Pitch:** Speak a civic problem in plain Tamil; instantly get back a formal, correctly-addressed petition — named officer, statutory deadline, tracking code.

**Universal core vs Tamil launch locale:** The product is a *restate-and-route normalization layer* that sits on top of any grievance backend: voice-in (colloquial, any language) → structured petition-out (right department, responsible officer, SLA, entitlement). Language-agnostic ASR, intent classification, and petition drafting are the core. Locale = one swappable config: the officer/SLA gazetteer. Tamil + Coimbatore ward table is just the first config; Marathi-Pune or Swahili-Nairobi is the same engine, new CSV.

**Pains it covers (breadth):**
- Mis-routing: colloquial voice/photo grievances land in the wrong department → intent classifier maps to correct dept + officer.
- No grounded answer on responsibility/timeline/entitlement → petition cites named officer + statutory deadline + citizen right.
- Literacy-gated forms block filing entirely → voice-only front door, zero typing.

**Evidence (hard point):** Tamil Nadu's Right to Public Services Act (2019) already fixes statutory time limits per service — the legal deadlines exist and are enforceable, but citizens can't map a spoken complaint to the right act/officer/clock. Sollu closes exactly that gap.

**Who + core loop:** Resident taps mic → speaks → hears+sees draft petition → confirms → routed to backend (or WhatsApp/PDF to office) → gets code → checks status by voice.

**AI stack:** Gemini (multimodal: Tamil ASR + photo evidence understanding + structured JSON petition), retrieval over officer/SLA gazetteer for grounding, React PWA (offline-queue, low-end Android, patchy-net tolerant), on-device TTS readback.

**36hr MVP slice:** ONE hero flow — Tamil voice → grounded routed petition + code for 3 Coimbatore departments (roads, water, sanitation). Built: full loop for these three. Vision (shown, not built): multi-language config swap, live backend write-back, status-by-voice.

**90-sec wow:** Judge speaks a messy Tanglish complaint aloud; 4 seconds later Sollu reads back a formal petition naming the actual Corporation officer and the legal deadline, with a QR-tracked code.

**Global scale path + TAM:** Every municipality on Earth runs grievance intake; config-swap = new market. Beyond TN: 20+ Indian states, then Global South govtech / civic-SaaS — a multi-billion-dollar public-sector market.

**Pilot/incubation:** TiE Kovai domain mentors validate the gazetteer; pilot in Coimbatore wards; incubation via Startup Culture.

**Why it wins / risks:** Wins on boldness + instant demo magic + genuine institution-strengthening. Risk: gazetteer accuracy and backend integration — mitigated by PDF/WhatsApp fallback needing zero government API.

# Nilai — DHO Review Copilot
**Track:** AI for Good — Health & Well-being · **Tag:** Safest Bet

**Pitch.** Drop a district's messy HMIS/RCH/stock exports in; get back a ranked, explained monthly-review agenda — which PHCs to fix first, why, and which numbers to distrust.

**Universal core vs Tamil launch locale.** *Generalizes:* a decision layer *above* any national health MIS — ingest heterogeneous exports, compute a composite facility score + data-quality flags, output a ranked, cited review agenda. The "trust these numbers, doubt those" sentinel over gamed field data is universal. *Locale only:* Tamil TTS briefs, TN HMIS/RCH schema, NHM indicator norms — a swappable skin.

**Pains it covers (breadth from one product).**
- Consumption/coverage monitoring incl. one stock item → surfaces stock-out risk
- Defaulter & low-coverage clusters ranked for follow-up
- Protocol-grounded decision support (root-cause narrative + data-distrust sentinel)

**Evidence (one hard point).** India's own HMIS routinely diverges from population surveys — NFHS-5 immunization/ANC coverage repeatedly contradicts administrative HMIS figures, and DPH data-quality reviews flag zero-reports and round-number entries. The gap officials already suspect is exactly what Nilai quantifies.

**Who uses it + core loop.** DHO/DDHS, Block Medical Officers, program officers prepping the monthly PHC review. Loop: export → ingest+normalize → score+flag → ranked top-5 agenda → drill-down to a concrete fix.

**AI stack.** Multimodal LLM (Gemini) for register-page OCR + schema/entity normalization; structured/function-calling for canonical indicator mapping; **deterministic** anomaly layer (z-score, Benford/round-number, MoM deltas) so flags are auditable, LLM only explains; RAG over NHM/RCH norms so every threshold cites an official number; Bhashini TTS/ASR for the Tamil audio brief.

**36hr MVP slice.** One district, ~15 PHCs, 3 indicators (immunization, ANC, one stock item). Hero flow: drop files → 15 PHCs self-rank → click top red PHC → see drivers + one Tamil talking point + playable audio brief. *Built:* single-district ranking + sentinel. *Vision:* multi-program, multi-district.

**90-sec wow.** Files in → live ranking → "why is Annur red?" → Tamil brief plays.

**Global scale path + TAM.** Buyers beyond TN: other Indian states (700+ districts), then any LMIC running DHIS2-class systems (WHO deploys DHIS2 in 70+ countries) — language-agnostic core, localized TTS.

**Pilot/incubation.** Read-only, PHI-free, aggregated → dodges procurement/security blockers. Pilot one TN block with a DDHS champion on 3 months of real exports; measure prep-time cut. TiE Kovai for DPH intros, GDG for enablement.

**Why it wins / risks.** Wins: zero-integration decision layer, not another dashboard; the distrust sentinel is the wedge. Risks: needs official data champion; handwritten-Tamil OCR needs human-in-loop; naming weak PHCs must read as supportive triage, not a league table.

*Note: intended evidence search was blocked (session web-search budget exhausted); the HMIS-vs-NFHS divergence point is from prior knowledge, not a fresh 2024-26 citation.*

# Kanakku — Build Spec

**Pitch:** A voice-first back-office that turns every logged sale, purchase and udhaar a micro-enterprise generates into a compounding "data passport" — then auto-assembles it into invoices, credit statements, and insurance claims that make thin-file borrowers bankable.

**Universal core vs Tamil launch locale**
*Generalizes:* the thin-file-to-bankable engine — voice/photo transaction capture → one structured financial-identity record → auto-generated billing + credit + claim artefacts. Informal economies exist everywhere; the passport mechanism is language- and regime-agnostic.
*Locale wiring (swappable):* Tamil ASR/TTS, GST HSN codes, PMFBY insurance rules, Agmarknet mandi feed, Indian scheme-eligibility logic. Each is a pluggable adapter, not the product.

**Pains it covers (breadth from ONE product)**
- Paper-and-cash back-office: can't bill, can't handle GST, can't see per-item profit
- Captured records go nowhere: no structured proof for loans, insurance, or schemes — the same data stream simultaneously bills, insures, and underwrites

**Evidence (one hard point):** India's MSME formal-credit gap is estimated near USD 530B (IFC), with ~85% of small enterprises un/under-served — precisely because they're "thin-file." The daily data that would fix this is generated and discarded.

**Who uses it + core loop:** Women-led SHGs, kiranas, smallholders (secondary: extension officers, NBFC/co-op loan officers). Loop: *speak/snap a transaction → confirm via TTS readback → ledger + profit update live → tap to emit invoice/loan-statement.*

**AI stack:** Bhashini Tamil ASR (IndicConformer) for voice-in; Gemini 2.0 Flash structured-output as reasoner (Tamil→ledger JSON, profit math, HSN classification, form-fill); Bhashini/Google TTS for readback; RAG over GST/scheme/mandi tables to ground codes and prices; Gemini vision for paper-bill photo capture. Reasoner and vision layers are locale-independent.

**36hr MVP slice (one hero flow):** *Tamil voice-in → money-out.* Speak a sale/udhaar → Gemini parses to a ledger line with TTS confirm → live receivables + per-item profit → one tap emits a GST-grounded invoice. *Built:* this slice. *Vision-shown:* offline sync, WhatsApp reminders, PMFBY.

**90-sec demo wow:** After a handful of spoken entries, tap "loan-ready" — Gemini drafts a 6-month cash-flow PDF from the same voice data. Private Tamil speech in, bankable artefact out.

**Global scale path + TAM:** Swap adapters for other Indian states/languages, then any informal economy (Southeast Asia, Africa, LatAm) — a billion+ thin-file micro-enterprises. Revenue: consented, aggregated cash-flow data licensed for thin-file underwriting — never charging the enterprise.

**Pilot/incubation:** Coimbatore SHG federation + kirana association via TiE Kovai; GDG for Bhashini/MeitY access; wire one co-op bank/NBFC to accept the artefact for Rs.50k–2L loans — the adoption proof.

**Why it wins / risks:** Cross-integration is the moat — the same proprietary voice stream bills, insures, and underwrites; a UI clone starts at zero history. *Risks:* ASR noise (mitigated by confirm-before-commit), HSN misclassification (RAG + review-flagged), and lender acceptance being a partnership — not tech — problem.

allConcepts.name: MaruthuVaani
allConcepts.angle: End-user / citizen tool: a phone-first Tamil audio+pictogram companion the patient uses on their own device, in scope as it 'assists healthcare workers in resource-constrained settings' by closing the post-consult adherence gap the PHC can't staff.
allConcepts.oneLiner: Snap your handwritten prescription and MaruthuVaani reads it back to you in plain Tamil — with a picture dose-card and voice reminders — so a patient who can't read still takes the right medicine at the right time.

allConcepts.name: Nilai — DHO Review Copilot
allConcepts.angle: Official / admin intelligence: sits ABOVE existing government systems, reads their messy exports, and turns them into ranked decisions for the officer — not another field data-entry app.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A district-health-officer decision dashboard that ingests messy HMIS/register exports from every PHC and outputs a ranked, explained monthly-review agenda — which facilities to fix first, why, and which numbers to distrust.

allConcepts.name: Nool
allConcepts.angle: Data-moat via cross-program identity resolution. Each capture stitches one de-duplicated, ABHA-keyed longitudinal record spanning programs that are siloed by design in the government stack. The vertical apps can each see only their own column; a worker-side capture layer that resolves the same person across all columns owns a graph none of them can replicate, and it compounds with every entry.
allConcepts.oneLiner: One Tamil voice capture per visit that de-duplicates the same human across every siloed government program (TB, ANC, NCD, immunization, drug dispensing) into a single longitudinal thread — a cross-program patient record no vertical govt app can structurally build.

allConcepts.name: PayirDesk
allConcepts.track: AI for Zero Hunger & Economic Growth
allConcepts.angle: Frontline-worker tool: treat the overloaded officer's attention as the scarce resource. Instead of a farmer-facing diagnosis toy, build the officer's triage console — AI auto-resolves the routine ~70%, and escalates only low-confidence/high-stakes cases as a ranked, clustered work queue. This is teletriage (intake → AI triage → escalate hard cases to the overloaded clinician) transplanted from telemedicine to agriculture.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil-first triage cockpit that lets one block Agricultural Officer supervise AI across 1,100+ farms — auto-closing routine leaf-disease cases and surfacing only the ranked, outbreak-clustered escalations.

allConcepts.name: Vayal Vaidhyar (Field Doctor)
allConcepts.track: AI for Zero Hunger & Economic Growth
allConcepts.angle: end-user / citizen tool — farmer uses it directly by camera + voice, no officer in the loop for the common case
allConcepts.oneLiner: Snap a leaf, hear the fix in Tamil — a phone-first crop doctor that names the disease AND tells the farmer the exact, safe spray dose, actively refusing to over-recommend.

allConcepts.name: Kaaval
allConcepts.track: AI for Zero Hunger & Economic Growth
allConcepts.angle: Official/admin intelligence layer that sits ON TOP of the farmer diagnosis apps: instead of diagnosing one more leaf, it clusters the incoming diagnoses into ranked outbreak decisions and closes the loop with an officer-approved Tamil broadcast — the missing 'officer brain' above tools like Plantix and the government's NPSS.
allConcepts.oneLiner: An outbreak-intelligence dashboard that turns the raw stream of farmers' leaf-photo diagnoses into a ranked, confidence-weighted triage queue of crop-disease outbreaks for a Block/District Agriculture Officer — with a one-tap Tamil voice advisory broadcast back to the affected villages.

allConcepts.name: Kanakku
allConcepts.track: AI for Zero Hunger & Economic Growth
allConcepts.angle: data-moat / novel integration: transaction history is inherently proprietary and sticky, so a longitudinal Tamil voice-logged ledger becomes a per-user credit passport a UI-cloning competitor starts at zero on. Kanakku deepens the moat by cross-integrating three feeds into ONE record per user — the enterprise's own voice-logged transactions (proprietary), plus grounded public rails (GST HSN/rate table, PMFBY spray/loss timeline, scheme eligibility rules, Agmarknet mandi prices) — so the same private data stream simultaneously bills, insures, and underwrites. No standalone ledger app (Khatabook/OkCredit) or disease-detection app (Plantix) owns that cross-wired, consented, Tamil-native dataset; it compounds monthly per user.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil voice-first back-office for SHGs, kiranas and smallholder farmers that turns every logged sale, purchase and udhaar into a compounding financial-identity record — the only structured cash-flow + agronomic history these thin-file borrowers have — and auto-assembles it into GST invoices, PMFBY claims, and loan-ready statements.

allConcepts.name: Veyyil Kaaval
allConcepts.track: AI for Sustainable Cities & Climate Action
allConcepts.angle: Frontline-worker tool: person-resolution, not ward-resolution. Instead of one more color-coded map, it fuses the ward heat-vulnerability layer with the worker's OWN registry of vulnerable individuals and hands her a short, ordered field worklist plus a spoken Tamil triage script — the broadcast warning becomes accountable, name-level action she completes on a low-end phone.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil-first PWA that turns a city heatwave warning into a named, ranked "check on these people today" worklist for the ward health worker, grounded in NDMA heat-illness protocol.

allConcepts.name: Veyil Kaaval
allConcepts.track: AI for Sustainable Cities & Climate Action
allConcepts.angle: End-user citizen tool: a low-literacy Tamil, phone-first heat companion. Reframes the track's "predictive heatwave alerts + heat-vulnerability index" from a municipal dashboard into a personal heat-ILLNESS early-warning the resident holds in their hand — the health-tech edge a telemedicine dev owns.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil voice-first PWA that turns city-wide heat warnings into a personal, hour-by-hour heat-illness risk plan keyed to your body, your job, and your specific ward's heat-island.

allConcepts.name: Kaaval Grid
allConcepts.track: AI for Sustainable Cities & Climate Action
allConcepts.angle: Official / admin intelligence: not another citizen AQI app (SAMEER already does that), but the enforcement action layer sitting on top of the pollution map — turning messy multi-source field signal into a ranked, defensible worklist and removing the reporting overhead that keeps skeleton staff off the field.
allConcepts.oneLiner: An enforcement-intelligence dashboard that fuses satellite thermal/smoke anomalies, ward-level AQI, and citizen complaints into a ranked weekly "inspect these units" worklist for the pollution-board officer — and auto-drafts the geotagged, rule-cited case record the moment they act.

allConcepts.name: VeppaNadi
allConcepts.track: AI for Sustainable Cities & Climate Action
allConcepts.angle: Data-moat via cross-integration no climate team can copy: fuse open environmental data (IMD/ERA5 forecast + satellite LST/NDVI + built density + income) with a geotagged, de-identified telemedicine syndromic signal — the ground-truth health-outcome layer. Environmental startups model who SHOULD be at risk; a telemedicine company uniquely knows who ACTUALLY got sick, per ward, in near-real-time. That closes the predict→verify→act loop and self-calibrates the vulnerability index.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil-first ward-level heatwave early-warning PWA whose heat-vulnerability index is calibrated and validated by live, de-identified telemedicine consult signals (heat-exhaustion, dehydration, respiratory spikes) — turning a static risk map into a self-tuning "health-adjusted heat risk" layer that tells a corporation which wards to shift labour hours and open cooling shelters today.

allConcepts.name: Niraivu — Ward Officer Closure Copilot
allConcepts.angle: Frontline-worker tool: instead of a punitive anomaly-detection layer that polices officers (adversarial), invert it — make AI do the officer's paperwork so the fastest way to clear a complaint is to actually resolve it with a geotagged before/after photo and a 5-second Tamil voice note. Compliance is a byproduct of a tool the worker genuinely wants.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil-first PWA for the ward-level sanitary inspector / junior engineer that hands them a de-duped, urgency-ranked work list and turns a spoken Tamil note plus an "after" photo into an AI-verified, audit-grade complaint closure — making honest closure faster than faking it.

allConcepts.name: Sollu (சொல்லு)
allConcepts.angle: End-user / citizen tool. Not a dashboard for staff and not a replacement for PGRS — a phone-first Tamil voice mouth-and-ear that sits ON TOP of the existing PGRS as a normalization/routing layer. Its signature move: the citizen speaks in colloquial Tamil and immediately hears their complaint read back as a formal, correctly-addressed petition, including the officer responsible and the deadline the law gives them. It turns a silent form into a two-way conversation that also teaches the citizen their entitlement.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil voice-first grievance front-door: the resident speaks or photographs a civic problem, and instantly hears back a structured, officially-routed petition with the responsible officer, the legal deadline, and a trackable code.

allConcepts.name: Theervu
allConcepts.angle: Official/admin intelligence: a read-only analytics layer on top of existing PGRS/CM Helpline exports that converts unstructured, duplicated, partly-falsified grievance data into a ranked ward dashboard plus an auto-generated accountability report — decisions, not just tickets.
allConcepts.oneLiner: An officer's decision cockpit that de-dupes messy citizen grievances into ranked ward priorities and exposes fake "resolved" closures, so a municipal officer sees the true unresolved load instead of a flat FIFO queue.

allConcepts.name: Saatchi
allConcepts.angle: Data-moat via novel cross-integration: the before/after geotagged proof-photo corpus is generated for free as a byproduct of closure verification, then joined to public works/tender expenditure data. Pure-intake apps never accumulate the ground-truth photo corpus; pure-RTI/budget dashboards have no ground truth. Only a tool that owns both can detect "money spent, no physical change." The corpus compounds ward-by-ward and cannot be back-filled by a copycat.
allConcepts.oneLiner: A Tamil-first civic evidence layer that turns citizen before/after geotagged photos into a proprietary public-works ledger, then cross-checks it against municipal expenditure records to expose ghost closures and ghost works.
